newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian shares end up aided by stable U.S. stocks.
newsitem.headline: Italian shares end up aided by stable U.S. stocks.

text.p: Milan shares closed about one percent higher on Tuesday, taking their cue from stability in U.S. stocks in early New York trading.
The all-share Mibtel Index rose 1.1 percent to 14,292, recouping part of Monday's two percent loss. The blue-chip Mib 30 Index ended up 1.1 percent at 21,534.

State-controlled Telecom Italia was the most actively traded stock, falling 0.83 percent to 10,680. Also active were savings shares of telephone directories publisher Seat, carmaker Fiat and state-controlled energy company Eni.

Business on the Italian exchange was slower than Monday, with volume totalling 946 billion lire ($526 million). Traders said foreign buyers were absent from lack of interest and the majority of domestic fund managers were on vacation.
Shares of textiles and clothing company Marzotto rose 2.8 percent to 17,490 after securities house Kleinwort Benson issued a buy recommendation on the stock with a target price of 21,000 lire.

Shares in Seat, which is controlled by the Italian Treasury, rose 1.3 percent after Telecom Italia said it would acquire 20 percent of the holding company that will control the publisher, paving the way for the completion of Seat's sale to a group led by Banca Commerciale Italiana.
The sale had been held up by lack of an agreement between Telecom Italia and buyers.
Banking shares were mixed and insurers were higher.
